;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[2019 India–Pakistan standoff]]
**Indian and Pakistani soldiers target each other’s posts and villages in Kashmir, killing at least six civilians and two Pakistani troops. [https://www.apnews.com/207c8bfb372640e9be2379d03c65ac05 (Associated Press)]
*[[Use of chemical weapons in the Syrian Civil War]]
**[[Douma chemical attack]]
***The [[OPCW Fact-Finding Mission in Syria|Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons's Fact-Finding Mission in Syria]] issues its report regarding the [[Douma chemical attack|April 7, 2018 chemical attack in Douma]]. It reveals that there is conclusive evidence that proves a toxic chemical containing molecular chlorine was used in the attack. However, it did not assign blame for the attack. Syrian President [[Bashar al-Assad]] and [[Syrian opposition|the opposition]] blame each other for the attack. [https://www.opcw.org/media-centre/news/2019/03/opcw-issues-fact-finding-mission-report-chemical-weapons-use-allegation (Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons)]
;Disasters and accidents
*At least 20 people are killed in flash floods in six districts including [[Kandahar City]], [[Afghanistan]]. [https://www.thehindu.com/news/international/flash-floods-in-afghanistan-kill-at-least-20/article26419766.ece (The Hindu)]
*Ten people are killed and 34 injured in three separate road accidents in [[Jammu and Kashmir (union territory)|Jammu-Kashmir]], [[India]]. [https://indianexpress.com/article/india/udhampur-bus-accident-dead-injured-5607855/?ref=archive_pg (The Indian Express)]
;International relations
*[[South Korea–United States relations]]
**The [[United States]] and [[South Korea]] announce that their annual large-scale exercises, commonly known as [[Foal Eagle]] and [[Key Resolve]], will end and will be re-configured into smaller exercises. The joint exercises will be done on a small unit level and may include virtual training similar to the 2018 exercises. [https://www.cnn.com/2019/03/02/politics/us-south-korea-military-exercises/index.html (CNN)]
;Law and crime
*Through a [[Decree|royal decree]], [[Salman of Saudi Arabia|King Salman of Saudi Arabia]] revokes the citizenship of [[Hamza bin Laden]], [[Osama bin Laden]]'s son, who works in the [[Al-Qaeda]] terrorist organization. The announcement comes after the United States government offered a reward of up to $1 million for information leading to the identification or location of him. [[Interpol]] has issued an [[Interpol notice]] for him after [[United Nations Security Council]] imposed sanctions on him which includes assets freeze, travel ban and arms embargo. He remains at large. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/saudi-arabia-revokes-hamza-bin-ladens-citizenship-this-is-an-example-of-history-rhyming-2019-03-02/ (CBS News)], [https://www.interpol.int/en/notice/search/un/6297888 (Interpol)], [https://www.un.org/press/en/2019/sc13726.doc.htm (United Nations Security Council)]
* Tashonty Toney, son of a police officer, was arrested for vehicular homicide, vehicular negligent injury, hit-and-run and reckless operation of a motor vehicle after he veered into a bike line near a Mardi Gras parade route in New Orleans. He accidentally killed 2 and injured 7 cyclists while drunk and drugged. [http://www.fox8live.com/2019/03/03/nopd-officers-son-accused-hit-and-run-crash-that-killed-injured/ (fox8live)] [https://www.theadvocate.com/new_orleans/news/courts/article_ae7e2f64-5194-11e9-a025-7b6291ccfde6.html (Advocate)]
;Politics and elections
* [[2019 Algerian presidential election]]
**Tens of thousands of Algerians take to streets to protest President [[Abdelaziz Bouteflika]]'s bid to seek re-election in [[2019 Algerian presidential election|2019 presidential election]] in what is Algeria's biggest anti-government protests since the [[2010–12 Algerian protests|2011 protests]]. 183 people have been injured. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-algeria-protests/183-injured-in-algeria-protests-state-news-agency-idUSKCN1QJ0ES (Reuters)]
*[[2019 Venezuelan presidential crisis]]
**[[Migración Colombia|Colombia's Immigration Authority]] states that 567 Venezuelan soldiers have defected to Colombia from [[Nicolás Maduro]]'s government since February 23, 2019. They were members of [[National Bolivarian Armed Forces of Venezuela|Venezuela's Armed Forces]] and [[Venezuelan National Police|Venezuela's National Police]]. [https://www.businessinsider.com/venezuela-soldiers-defect-to-colombia-threaten-maduro-power-2019-3 (''Business Insider'')], [https://cnnespanol.cnn.com/2019/02/28/mas-de-500-militares-venezolanos-han-dejado-sus-puestos-y-han-cruzado-a-colombia-segun-autoridades-migratorias/ (CNN Spanish)]
;Science and technology
*[[2019 in spaceflight]]
**[[SpaceX]] launches the first [[Dragon 2|Crew Dragon]] spacecraft to the [[International Space Station]] as part of the [[SpX-DM1|Crew Dragon Demo-1]] mission, with the first stage of its [[Falcon 9]] launch vehicle making a successful landing on the drone ship ''[[Autonomous spaceport drone ship#Of Course I Still Love You|Of Course I Still Love You]]''. [https://www.nytimes.com/2019/03/01/science/spacex-crew-dragon-launch.html (''The New York Times'')]
